summary: Learn practical AI bias assessment, fairness metrics, and governance methods for HR and public-service decisions. Explore the course.
lede: Inclusive AI and data governance training helps teams review automated decisions for inequitable effects. It is designed for DEI leaders, HR analytics professionals, data scientists, and policy or compliance staff who assess decisions in hiring, promotion, customer engagement, and public services. Participants practise reviewing dataset representation, comparing fairness measures, mapping stakeholder recourse, and documenting oversight through review records and governance controls.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who assess, govern, or oversee AI-supported decisions affecting employees, customers, or people using public services. This course is designed for: DEI leaders translating inclusion commitments into AI review criteria. HR analytics specialists checking hiring and promotion outcomes by demographic group. Talent acquisition managers overseeing automated candidate screening workflows. People data scientists assessing representation, label quality, and model outputs. AI governance officers maintaining risk registers and review records. Compliance officers examining fairness controls in automated decision processes. Responsible AI specialists coordinating impact assessments and human oversight. Social protection policy advisors reviewing eligibility and service-prioritization systems. Customer analytics leads testing segmentation and service-access outcomes for bias. Internal auditors evaluating evidence for AI equity and accountability controls.
modules: NIST AI RMF and Equity Risks
ISO AI Governance and Ethical Review
prerequisites: Working familiarity with at least one of these areas is useful: DEI practice, HR or talent analytics, data analysis, compliance, AI governance, or public policy. Programming is not required. Advanced model development and statistical implementation are covered at conceptual awareness level.
